text:
maria (support): Hey team — escalating a customer p99 spike after onboarding a new variant. Customer: alex@acme says p99 went from ~240ms to ~1.6s for long-context requests (>8k tokens) after we activated cerberus-2b-long yesterday. Root report attached: logs + short repro. They say this started exactly after model activation.

alex (customer): repro steps:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"model":"cerberus-2b-long","input":"<8k tokens sequence>...","max_tokens":64}'
2) use conversation state with prefix caching
Observed: stable 220ms p95 before, now p99 ~1.6s, intermittently spikes to 2.1s. No 5xx, responses are correct.

maria (support): @tariq @liam can you triage? Customer needs mitigation while we investigate. They are on Dedicated with reserved pool.

tariq (eng-runtime): Looking. Any request ids / traces? Also, did they switch tokenizer settings (byte align vs legacy) during onboarding?

alex (customer): we used the onboarding config from console, didn't change tokenizer. Trace ids: trace=tr_01F8ABCDEF (attached). Sample request id: req_20260311_9982

liam (eng-ml): preliminary theory: the long variant uses a different BPE merge table that changes token boundaries for some CJK/pseudo-binary sequences -> more tokens -> KV cache behavior changes and peaks in batching. But single-request p99 rising that much suggests runtime path change (e.g., slow tokenization path or fallback to software tokenization) or a KVCACHE invalidation causing recompute.

tariq (eng-runtime): I pulled traces. Saw durations: tokenization 1.2s in slow cases, model decode 180ms. So tokenization is culprit. Sample profiler snippet:
```
[profiling] req=req_20260311_9982
tokenize: 1234ms
serialize: 12ms
runtime: 178ms
```

maria (support): wow. Any quick mitigation we can apply for customer? They need p99 <500ms.

tariq (eng-runtime): Two options: 1) revert model activation to previous non-long variant for that customer (fast but downgrades context) 2) force server-side fast tokenizer (legacy byte-level) until we patch the software tokenizer. Will need a short hotfix to disable software fallback.

liam (eng-ml): Also want to check if the new merge table triggered the slow path in our tokenizer lib due to unusual unicode combining sequences. If we can reproduce locally, we can patch early.

maria (support): @ops-bot can you roll a canary revert for this customer while eng investigates? Customer agreed to temporary downgrade.

ops-bot: Starting canary rollback: id=rb_2130123600 target=acme-corp-owner. Will route traffic to cerberus-2b (non-long). ETA ~3m. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Noted. No infra errors.

alex (customer): thanks, will confirm after routing change.

~5m later

alex (customer): routing applied, p99 back to 260ms. Thanks.

maria (support): Great. For root cause: @liam can you reproduce tokenization slowdown with our tokenizer harness? If so, please file a patch.

liam (eng-ml): Reproduced with dataset that includes long emoji sequences + high combining marks. Cause: new BPE table introduced splits sequences into more but longer codepoint clusters; our tokenization engine attempts a normalization step that falls back to Python-based regex for certain byte patterns. That fallback is 1.1s for 8k context. Filed GH: rwd-tokenizer-142 with patch idea: precompute UTF-8 fast-path and short-circuit the regex. Patch diff attached.

liam (eng-ml): Patch perf locally: tokenization -> 28ms, total p99 -> 210ms. Will push hotfix to staging and then prod. Need runtime team to help deploy.

tariq (eng-runtime): Will pick up hotfix. Quick patch plan: insert feature flag TOKENIZER_FASTPATH=true for prod for affected region or customer routing. Then roll across pool, monitor p99.

maria (support): Estimated ETA to full rollout?

tariq (eng-runtime): hotfix branch -> staging -> canary -> prod for that Dedicated pool. ~2 hours assuming no surprises.

alex (customer): appreciate the fast turn. We'll keep monitoring. Any user-visible behavior changes (text splitting, scoring)?

liam (eng-ml): Patch only affects internal implementation, not BPE table or decode; outputs identical. We'll add regression tests with their canonical prompts.

maria (support): I'll keep threads updated and schedule a postmortem after full deploy. Anything else?

tariq (eng-runtime): One more ask: product/console team — add a flag on onboarding flow to "validate tokenizer perf against sample corpus" to catch this earlier.

maria (support): good idea. @product

end of thread.
